questions.title: Section A - Multiple Choice, Terminology, Matching, DNA Replication and a Dihybrid Cross

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following organelles is the site of protein synthesis?
A) Ribosomes
B) Chloroplasts
C) Mitochondria
D) Centrosomes
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: A (2 marks)
Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis (translation).

subQuestions.questionText:
In humans, the gonosomes determine the gender. Which combination below shows the CORRECT gonosomes for males and females?
A) Male gonosomes: XY; Female gonosomes: YY
B) Male gonosomes: YY; Female gonosomes: XY
C) Male gonosomes: XY; Female gonosomes: XX
D) Male gonosomes: XX; Female gonosomes: XY
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Males have XY gonosomes and females have XX gonosomes.

options.A: Male gonosomes: XY; Female gonosomes: YY
options.B: Male gonosomes: YY; Female gonosomes: XY
options.C: Male gonosomes: XY; Female gonosomes: XX
options.D: Male gonosomes: XX; Female gonosomes: XY

subQuestions.questionText:
An organism has the genotype TT. The CORRECT term which describes this organism's genotype is …
A) heterozygous dominant.
B) heterozygous recessive.
C) homozygous dominant.
D) homozygous recessive.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
TT has two identical dominant alleles, so it is homozygous dominant.

subQuestions.questionText:
Down syndrome is a genetic disorder where an individual has an extra copy of chromosome 21. Which ONE of the following may lead to Down syndrome?
A) Failure of chromosomes to replicate during mitosis
B) Failure of chromosome pairs to separate during meiosis
C) Failure of chromosomes to form pairs during fertilisation
D) Failure of chromosome pairs to cross over during meiosis
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Failure of chromosome pairs to separate (non-disjunction) during meiosis can produce a gamete with an extra copy of chromosome 21.

options.A: Failure of chromosomes to replicate during mitosis
options.B: Failure of chromosome pairs to separate during meiosis
options.C: Failure of chromosomes to form pairs during fertilisation
options.D: Failure of chromosome pairs to cross over during meiosis

subQuestions.questionText:
A gradual change in the characteristics of a species over time is known as …
A) punctuated equilibrium.
B) genetic engineering.
C) speciation.
D) biological evolution.
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
A gradual change in the characteristics of a species over time is biological evolution.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is a reproductive isolation mechanism?
A) Adaptation to the same pollinator
B) Species-specific courtship behaviour
C) Production of fertile offspring
D) Breeding at the same time of the year
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: B (2 marks)
Species-specific courtship behaviour is a reproductive (pre-zygotic) isolation mechanism.

options.D: Breeding at the same time of the year

subQuestions.questionText:
Analysis of mitochondrial DNA is an example of this line of evidence:
A) Fossil evidence
B) Modification by descent
C) Biogeography
D) Genetic evidence
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: D (2 marks)
Analysis of mitochondrial DNA is genetic evidence for evolution.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which option in the table below shows the CORRECT comparison between mitosis and meiosis?
A) Mitosis: Produces four daughter cells; Meiosis: Produces two daughter cells
B) Mitosis: Produces genetically different cells; Meiosis: Produces genetically identical cells
C) Mitosis: The chromosome number remains the same; Meiosis: The chromosome number is halved
D) Mitosis: Two divisions occur; Meiosis: Four divisions occur
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
In mitosis the chromosome number remains the same, while in meiosis the chromosome number is halved.

options.A: Mitosis: Produces four daughter cells; Meiosis: Produces two daughter cells
options.B: Mitosis: Produces genetically different cells; Meiosis: Produces genetically identical cells
options.C: Mitosis: The chromosome number remains the same; Meiosis: The chromosome number is halved
options.D: Mitosis: Two divisions occur; Meiosis: Four divisions occur

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following scientists discovered the fossil Taung Child?
A) Lee Berger
B) Ron Clarke
C) Raymond Dart
D) Robert Broom
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
Raymond Dart discovered the Taung Child fossil.

subQuestions.questionText:
Which ONE of the following is produced at the end of translation?
A) A DNA molecule
B) A messenger RNA molecule
C) A protein
D) An amino acid
subQuestions.memoText:
Correct answer: C (2 marks)
A protein is produced at the end of translation.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN II.
Description: A source of variation in populations.
A: Random fertilisation
B: Random mating
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B ✓✓ (2 marks)
Both random fertilisation and random mating are sources of variation in populations.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN II.
Description: Discovery of the structure of the DNA molecule.
A: Franklin and Wilkins
B: Lamarck and Darwin
subQuestions.memoText:
A only ✓✓ (2 marks)
Franklin and Wilkins were involved in the discovery of the structure of the DNA molecule.

subQuestions.questionText:
Indicate whether the description applies to A ONLY, B ONLY, BOTH A AND B or NONE of the items in COLUMN II.
Description: Occurs during meiosis.
A: Karyokinesis
B: Cytokinesis
subQuestions.memoText:
Both A and B ✓✓ (2 marks)
Both karyokinesis (nuclear division) and cytokinesis (cytoplasmic division) occur during meiosis.

Name the type of dominance shown by the inheritance of blood group A.
subQuestions.memoText: Complete ✓ dominance (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain how it is possible for a man with blood group A and a woman with blood group AB to have a child with blood group B.
subQuestions.memoText:
(5):
- The man is heterozygous ✓/is I^A i for blood group A
- The woman has an allele for blood group B ✓/is I^A I^B
- The child inherits the I^B allele from the mother ✓
- and the i allele from the father ✓
- Therefore, the child will be heterozygous ✓ for blood group B/the genotype will be I^B i

Guideline for assessing the graph (6):

subQuestions.questionText:
The pedigree diagram in the question paper shows the inheritance of muscular dystrophy in a family. Muscular dystrophy is a genetic condition caused by a recessive allele on the X chromosome (X^d); the dominant allele (X^D) results in normal muscle formation. Key: Male without muscular dystrophy, Female without muscular dystrophy, Male with muscular dystrophy, Female with muscular dystrophy. How many offspring do individuals 1 and 2 have?
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText: Three ✓/3 (1)

subQuestions.questionText:
Give the:
(a) Phenotype of individual 1
(b) Genotype of individual 2
(Refer to the diagram in the question paper.)
subQuestions.memoText:
(a) Male without muscular dystrophy ✓ (1)
(b) X^D X^d ✓ (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why more males than females are likely to have muscular dystrophy.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any (4):
- Males only have one X chromosome ✓/XY and
- need only one recessive allele to have muscular dystrophy ✓
- The X^d allele on a male cannot be masked by a dominant allele ✓
- Females have two X-chromosomes ✓ and
- need two recessive alleles to have muscular dystrophy ✓/X^d X^d
- In females, a dominant allele on one X chromosome would mask the effect of the recessive allele ✓/X^D masks X^d

25 ✓* % chance of a muscular dystrophy child

subQuestions.memoText:
Any (3):

- This recombinant DNA ✓

subQuestions.questionText:
Researchers investigated the influence of the type of milk on the height of children over 7 years (from age 3 to age 10). Each group had the same additional diet, similar daily activities and similar living conditions, with milk provided from the same supplier. The children's average height was measured at the end. Results (cm): expected average height 149,86; average height on cow's milk 151,4; average height on soy milk 147,4.
Identify the:
(a) Independent variable
(b) Dependent variable
subQuestions.memoText:

(b) Height ✓ of children (1)

subQuestions.questionText: Name the type of variation displayed by the height of a person.

- Ensure similar living conditions ✓

- Design the recording sheet ✓
- Decide on the source of milk ✓

(2):

Read the passage: In 1986 there was a huge radioactive disaster in Chernobyl and all humans immediately left the area because of the deadly high radiation. subQuestions.questionText: Use Darwin's theory of natural selection to explain the development of immunity to cancer in these wolves.

Any (7):
- There was variation amongst (the population of) the wolves ✓
- Some had the mutation which made them immune to cancer and some did not ✓
- When exposed to radiation ✓
- the wolves without the mutation/immunity died ✓
- Those with the mutation/immunity survived ✓
- and reproduced ✓
- passing the allele for the mutation/immunity to their offspring ✓
- The next generation had a higher proportion of wolves with the mutation ✓/immunity to cancer
